cards.info: What does the absolute value of a number represent on a number line?
cards.backInfo: Absolute value represents the distance of a number or expression from zero on the number line.

cards.info: What is the first step in solving an absolute-value equation or inequality?
cards.backInfo: The first step is to isolate the absolute-value expression on one side of the operator.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps: Isolate the absolute value, Split into two cases, Solve linear parts, and Combine solutions.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/e6242ee8-102b-4abb-8316-8d3591e6da3b-1786505622357-377.webp)

cards.info: Into which two linear equations should $|ax + b| = c$ be split?
cards.backInfo: It must be split into $ax + b = c$ and $ax + b = -c$.

cards.info: Does the inequality $|ax + b| < c$ result in an AND or OR solution?
cards.backInfo: It results in an intersection (AND) of solutions because the distance from zero is small.

cards.info: Does the inequality $|ax + b| > c$ result in an AND or OR solution?
cards.backInfo: It results in a union (OR) of solutions because the distance from zero is large.

cards.info: When splitting $|ax + b| > c$, what is the negative case inequality?
cards.backInfo: The negative case requires reversing the inequality sign to $ax + b < -c$.

cards.info: How can you verify the solution to an absolute-value inequality?
cards.backInfo: Test one value inside the resulting interval and one value outside the interval in the original expression.

cards.info: What is the solution for an isolated absolute value less than a negative number?
cards.backInfo: There is no real solution because an absolute value is always non-negative.

cards.info: What is the solution for an isolated absolute value greater than a negative number?
cards.backInfo: The solution is all real numbers because an absolute value is always $\ge 0$.

cards.info: How do solution intervals differ between 'less than' and 'greater than' absolute-value inequalities?
cards.backInfo: 'Less than' results in a single bounded interval; 'greater than' results in two separate rays pointing in opposite directions.

cards.info: If $|x| = 5$, what is the geometric interpretation regarding the number line?
cards.backInfo: The value $x$ is exactly 5 units away from zero in either direction.

cards.info: In the equation $3|x - 2| + 4 = 10$, what must be moved first?
cards.backInfo: Subtract 4 from both sides, then divide by 3 to isolate the bars.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps: Isolate the absolute value, Split into two cases, Solve linear parts, and Combine solutions.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/e6242ee8-102b-4abb-8316-8d3591e6da3b-1786505622357-377.webp)

cards.info: Solve $|x + 5| = 2$ by identifying the two resulting linear equations.
cards.backInfo: The two equations are $x + 5 = 2$ and $x + 5 = -2$.

cards.info: Why does $|x| < 3$ result in the compound inequality $-3 < x < 3$?
cards.backInfo: It represents all points whose distance from zero is less than 3 units.

cards.info: What mnemonic helps remember that $|x| > c$ uses a union of solutions?
cards.backInfo: Think 'Great-OR' to remember that 'greater than' symbols require an OR (union) solution.

cards.info: When splitting $|2x - 1| \ge 7$, what are the two resulting inequalities?
If a solution is $-2 < x < 4$, why test $x = 5$?
cards.backInfo: To verify that values outside the interval make the original inequality false.

cards.info: Is the expression $-2|x + 3|$ equivalent to $|-2x - 6|$?
cards.backInfo: No; you cannot distribute a negative multiplier into absolute value bars.

cards.info: Why does $|x + 10| < -1$ have no solution?
cards.backInfo: An absolute value represents distance, which can never be less than a negative.

cards.info: What is the solution set for $|5x - 2| \ge -3$?
cards.backInfo: All real numbers, because any absolute value is always greater than or equal to zero.
